subject: Priority Support Transition & SLA Banding — Renewal Proposal
messages:
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Priority Support Transition & SLA Banding — Renewal Proposal

Hi Evan / Priya,

Thanks again for the productive renewal call yesterday. As promised, I put together a concise proposal for the support & SLO changes you asked about so your product team can keep its launch cadence through Q4. High level: a priority-support upgrade (24/7 incident phone + 1-hour P1 response, named oncall rotation), a small retainer for burst capacity credits, and a tightened latency SLO band for your two main endpoints.

Key points in this note:
- Proposed SLOs: 95th pctl latency <= 350ms for short-text generate (<=128 tokens); 95th pctl latency <= 450ms for long-text generate (129-2048 tokens); embeddings 99th pctl <= 120ms.
- Retainer: $25k/month retainer applied as credits toward burst GPUs and engineering time; retains priority escalation paths and 4x faster operational runbooks.
- Oncall and runbook: named oncall with a primary/secondary rotation, weekly warm-handoff for first 8 weeks post-rollout, and quarterly playbook reviews.
- Contract mechanics: term extends one year from renewal date with an addendum (attached draft). Pricing uplift is 18% on committed usage for the premium tier, with the retainer offset for the first two quarters.

Attachments: Redwood_Premium_Addendum_v1.pdf (draft), Capacity-Forecast-Q3-Q4-2025.xlsx (example credit deck).

Next steps I propose:
1) Evan/Priya: confirm the SLO targets above are aligned with what Luminexa can commit to for production traffic.
2) Lauren/Monica: if Luminexa agrees, we'll circulate an addendum for legal + procurement and prepare a DocuSign.
3) Schedule a 30-min ops alignment (suggested: Jun 20) to walk the runbook and warm-handoff cadence.

Happy to adjust the SLO bands if you want different percentile targets or separate baselines by region.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Karthik — thanks for the write-up and quick turnaround. A few clarifying questions from our side: 

1) The 95th pctl values look reasonable for our short-text traffic, but for batch inference (large batched job runs overnight) we usually accept higher tail latency. Can you confirm the SLO will only apply to on-demand API calls and exclude scheduled batch jobs?

2) The retainer model makes sense — can you share an example of how credits would be consumed (e.g., credits -> burst GPU hours -> infra vs engineer time)? We want to understand how that lines up with our internal chargeback.

3) On the oncall: is the 1-hour P1 response measured as acknowledgement or as actionable remediation? We need clear handoff SLA since our product ops team will be first responder.

We like the 30-min ops alignment — Jun 20 works for Priya and me.

Thanks,
Evan Morales
Head of Platform Engineering, Luminexa
evan@luminexa.com

Looping in procurement/finance and legal notes. Evan — quick answers to your questions from our side:

- SLO scope: We typically scope latency SLOs to online request paths (production API endpoints). We'll include an explicit exclusion clause for scheduled batch jobs and backfill windows in the addendum.
- Retainer credit flows: the retainer is applied first to operational burst usage (GPU hours), then to prioritized engineering blocks (post-incident fixes or prioritized backlog). We track credit consumption and provide monthly statements so your chargeback team has visibility.
- P1 response: industry practice (and what we propose) is acknowledgement within 1 hour and an incident playbook entry/action within 4 hours depending on severity. We can make the acknowledgment window contractual and keep remediation windows in the runbook.

I've attached a redline checklist for procurement items and added a note about tax/compliance fields the legal team will need. Happy to take these offline with Priya if you prefer.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Evan / Priya — thanks for the quick feedback. Below are concrete clarifications and a small adjustment to the addendum before we send to legal: 

- Scope: Confirmed — SLOs apply only to online API traffic. We'll add a specific exclusion clause for scheduled batch jobs, bulk re-embeddings, and training/finetune workloads.
- Credit consumption example (illustrative): $25k retainer/month = 1000 burst GPU hours @ listed rate OR up to 40 prioritized engineering hours. That means typical usage for a single burst event (24h spike) would consume ~120 credits and the remainder rolls forward for the quarter. We'll include a sample monthly statement template in the support portal.
- P1 behavior: we'll contractize "acknowledgement within 1 hour" and keep remediation milestones in the runbook: P1 action plan within 4 hours, P2 initial triage within 3 hours during business window.

Action items:
- Monica: can you attach the addendum with the exclusion clause and the credit consumption examples (I updated the draft)?
- Evan/Priya: confirm you are good to proceed with these clarifications so we can route the addendum to legal. If yes, we'll also schedule the ops alignment meeting for Jun 20 at 10:00 AM PT (calendar invite pending).

Thanks — I'll stand by for confirmation.
Karthik
